subject.title: [Feature]: Support multi-target cron delivery from configured target sets

question: Which durable public contract should cron use for multi-target announce delivery: explicit per-job targets only, a maintainer-managed named target-set mechanism, or both with a deliberately bounded initial scope?
rationale: This choice determines persisted cron schema, operator configuration, audit semantics, authorization boundaries, and upgrade behavior; it cannot be safely inferred from the closed unmerged proposals.

options.title: Explicit targets first
options.body: Add an additive per-job target list while retaining the current single-target fields, and defer named target sets until their ownership and configuration model are approved.

options.title: Approve target sets too
options.body: Define a separately owned configuration contract for named target sets and specify delivery-time resolution, authorization, and audit behavior before implementation.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep the request open but postpone implementation until proactive-context and concurrent session-write policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Explicit targets first
recommendation.body: Add an additive per-job target list while retaining the current single-target fields, and defer named target sets until their ownership and configuration model are approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing destination-session delivery path is the closest merged implementation boundary for deciding how each successful fan-out target must be recorded safely.
